tagline: Pioneering wireless technologies and chipsets for the connected intelligent edge
hero_kpi_rationale: The 16% growth in the QCT (equipment) segment highlights Qualcomm's strategic positioning in premium smartphone, IoT and automotive chips.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Gross Margin — gross profit divided by revenue.
kpis.description: Gross margin declined to 55% in 2025 from 56% in 2024, primarily due to a lower share of revenues from licensing (QTL), which carries higher margins

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Calculated from operating income (revenue minus costs minus R&D), the operating margin is approximately 18.5% in 2025. This estimate requires validation as the $5.7 Bn tax expense impacts net income but not directly operating income.

kpis.name: R&D as % Revenue
kpis.description: R&D expenses reached $9.0 Bn in 2025, representing 20% of revenues, up in absolute value (+$149 M) but down as a percentage from 23% in 2024, due to faster revenue growth (+14%).

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue — total sales generated over the period.
kpis.description: Total revenue reached $44.3B in 2025, up 14% from $39.0B in 2024, driven by growth in the QCT segment (equipment and services), which increased 16%.

kpis.name: QCT Equipment Revenue
kpis.description: The QCT (Qualcomm CDMA Technologies) segment generated $37.9 B in revenue in 2025, up 16% (+$5.1 B) year-on-year, driven by stronger demand in handsets, IoT, and automotive.

kpis.name: QTL Licensing Revenue
kpis.description: The QTL (Qualcomm Technology Licensing) segment reported revenues of $6.4 B in 2025, an increase of $244 M (+4%) compared to $6.2 B in 2024, including $143 M from a litigation settlement in the second quarter.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last eight reported fiscal years (10-K)

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net Income — bottom-line profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL for the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Dividend Per Share — total dividends paid divided by shares outstanding.
kpis.description: Dividend per share paid annually, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend cut risk, monitor payout sustainability

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.explanation: Capital Return — total cash returned to shareholders (dividends + buybacks).
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Payout Ratio — dividends paid divided by net income.
kpis.description: Payout ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Shareholder returns growing, dividend policy supportive

stories_kpis.name: Net Income
stories_kpis.explanation: Final profit after all fees, taxes, and charges.
stories_kpis.description: Net income drops to $5.5B in 2025 from $10.1B in 2024, due to an exceptional tax charge of $5.7B related to the write-down of deferred tax assets following the adoption of the OBBB reform in July 2025.
stories_kpis.signal: Decline in net income in 2025 despite sales growth, due to an exceptional tax charge of $5.7 B

stories_kpis.name: One-time Tax Charge
stories_kpis.explanation: One-time loss related to a tax reform impacting future assets.
stories_kpis.description: In Q4 2025, QCOM recorded a $5.7 Bn charge to establish a valuation allowance against federal deferred tax assets following the adoption of the OBBB (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) on July 4, 2025, which introduces the CAMT tax starting in 2026.
stories_kpis.signal: Major impact of U.S. tax reform (OBBB) on 2025 profitability, with CAMT introduction starting in 2026.

ai_positioning.summary: The company QCOM does not explicitly mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report.

risks.title: Impairment of deferred tax assets
risks.summary: Due to the new corporate minimum tax (CAMT), QCOM had to establish a $5.7 Bn valuation allowance against its deferred tax assets, threatening their future recoverability.
risks.score_rationale: Risk is mentioned as resulting in a $5.7 billion charge in 2025 due to CAMT, a major regulatory change. The language is categorical ("no longer expect to realize substantially all"). The Capital category is heavily weighted here. This risk is new and existential for the tax structure. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Estimations comptables incertaines
risks.summary: Accounting estimates, particularly on royalties, inventories, and taxes, involve inherent uncertainty that could significantly impact financial results.
risks.score_rationale: The risk factor is repeated across multiple line items (revenues, inventories, taxes, assets). Although variances were marginal in 2024-2025, the document highlights that differences could be "material". Central position in the 10-K and cautious language. (default score, subject to refinement)

risks.title: Risks related to unlisted investments
risks.summary: Investments in privately-held technology startups are exposed to impairment risks in the event of funding difficulties or weak market performance.
risks.score_rationale: Portfolio of $1.4B across 150 companies, often early-stage. The text highlights risks of illiquidity, depreciation, and stock market impacts. Although no significant losses have been recorded, the risk is structural and recurring. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Litiges juridiques et réglementaires
risks.summary: QCOM faces legal and regulatory proceedings with uncertain outcomes, potentially leading to significant financial losses not fully reserved.
risks.score_rationale: The document indicates that potential losses could exceed provisions, and that outcomes are 'inherently uncertain'. Explicit mention of exposure to physical losses. Recurring risk of high intensity. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Exchange rate fluctuations
risks.summary: Currency fluctuations, particularly in the Korean won, can significantly impact results, especially through the large recoverable tax item in Korea.
risks.score_rationale: Exposure of $2.2B to tax receivables in Korea: a 10% change in rates would cost $223M. The risk is quantified and active, but partially hedged. Mentioned in market risks. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Dépréciation des stocks
risks.summary: A decline in demand or market changes could force QCOM to write down its inventory, reducing its gross margin.
risks.score_rationale: Risk is linked to customer demand and macroeconomic conditions. Although recent impact has been <1%, the text highlights a margin compression risk if demand collapses. Industrial category, moderate intensity. (default score, to be refined)

governance.voting_structure_note: Single class of common stock, 1 vote per share.
